decisions.question: Which exported functions and classes does the facade offer?
decisions.answer: MediaAirplayButton, MediaCaptionsButton, MediaCastButton, MediaChromeButton, MediaChromeDialog, MediaChromeRange, MediaControlBar, MediaController, MediaDurationDisplay, MediaErrorDialog, MediaKeyboardShortcutsDialog, MediaFullscreenButton, MediaGestureReceiver, MediaLiveButton, MediaLoadingIndicator, MediaMuteButton, MediaPipButton, MediaPlaybackRateButton, MediaLoopButton, MediaPlayButton, MediaPosterImage, MediaPreviewChapterDisplay, MediaPreviewThumbnail, MediaPreviewTimeDisplay, MediaSeekBackwardButton, MediaSeekForwardButton, MediaTimeDisplay, MediaTimeRange, MediaTooltip, MediaVolumeRange, MediaContainer, MediaTextDisplay

decisions.question: Which upstream failures become which tagged errors?
decisions.why: kept: media-chrome exports no error class; a media failure is the media element's `error` (shown by <media-error-dialog>), not a thrown error, and the frontend facade wraps no call

decisions.question: Which handles are provided as services (Context.Service with a layer)?
decisions.why: kept: a frontend facade binds the manifest's elements and reads no handle (src/ui-facade.ts); an element lives as long as its place in the view, so nothing is acquired or released

decisions.question: Which of media-chrome's elements does the frontend facade offer?
decisions.answer: every element in the manifest but media-container and media-keyboard-shortcuts-dialog
decisions.why: media-container is the base class of <media-controller> (media-controller.ts extends it) and holds no media store on its own; <media-controller> creates its own <media-keyboard-shortcuts-dialog> when `?` is pressed (media-controller.ts:932). The base elements (media-chrome-button, -range, -dialog, -menu, -menu-item, -menu-button, media-text-display) stay: upstream documents them for building custom controls. No element is marked deprecated in the source

decisions.question: Which element properties does the facade leave out?
decisions.answer: tooltipEl on every button; innerHTML and textContent on the displays and playback-rate buttons; breakpointsComputed and userInteractive on media-controller
decisions.why: tooltipEl holds the button's own <media-tooltip>, set in connectedCallback. innerHTML and textContent are misread by the manifest's analyzer from `this.#slot.textContent = ...` and `this.container.innerHTML = ...`; setting the element's own would replace the children the view renders. breakpointsComputed is the container's internal flag (media-container.ts:300), and userInteractive reflects the `userinactive` attribute the container sets itself on autohide. The media* state properties stay: upstream calls them read-only (the controller writes them), but a control used without a controller is driven by them

decisions.question: Which elements are typed `Record<string, unknown>` because upstream's types do not name them?
decisions.why: media-chrome 4.19.5 declares no `HTMLElementTagNameMap` (nor `GlobalEventHandlersEventMap`) entry in its .d.ts files: every property is typed unknown and every event's detail unknown. Upstream should declare them; reported

decisions.question: Which revision of this upstream version is the facade?
decisions.why: engine 0.2.0: the package ships its agent skill (SKILL.md) and a README with examples taken from its passing tests and the install URL of its newest release
